questions.question_text:
A breakfast deal at a cafe is one of $8$ pastries with one of $5$ hot drinks.
How many different breakfast deals are possible?

options.why: Added the two counts instead of multiplying, which counts the items on offer rather than the deals.
Multiplied the pastries by the number of stages ($8 \times 2$) instead of by the number of drinks.
Counted only the pastry choices and ignored the drink stage altogether.

questions.solution_text:
There are $8$ ways to choose the pastry and $5$ ways to choose the drink.
$8 \times 5$
$= 40$

questions.question_text:
A burger shop combo is one burger, one side and one drink.
There are $5$ burgers, $3$ sides and $4$ drinks.
How many different combos are possible?

options.why: Added the three counts instead of multiplying them together.
Multiplied only the burgers and the sides, leaving out the drink stage.
Multiplied only the burgers and the drinks, leaving out the side stage.

questions.solution_text:
There are $5$ burgers, $3$ sides and $4$ drinks.
$5 \times 3 \times 4$
$= 60$

questions.question_text:
A padlock uses a $4$-digit code.
Each digit may be any of the digits $0$ to $9$, and digits may be repeated.
How many different codes are possible?

options.why: Reduced the count at each position ($10 \times 9 \times 8 \times 7$), assuming a digit could not be used twice.
Used only three positions, forgetting that the code has four digits.
Multiplied the $10$ digits by the $4$ positions instead of using $10$ once for each position.

questions.solution_text:
Each of the four positions has $10$ options, because digits may be repeated.
$10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$
$= 10\,000$

questions.question_text:
A membership card number is $2$ letters followed by $3$ digits, and letters and digits may be repeated.
How many different card numbers are possible?

options.why: Reduced each count by one along the way ($26 \times 25 \times 10 \times 9 \times 8$), assuming no letter or digit could repeat.
Used only two digit positions instead of the three the card number has.
Multiplied the $26$ letters by the $2$ letter positions instead of using $26$ once for each position.

questions.solution_text:
Each letter position has $26$ options and each digit position has $10$.
$26 \times 26 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$
$= 676 \times 1000$
$= 676\,000$

questions.question_text:
A pizza deal is one pizza with one side.
There are $9$ pizzas and $6$ sides on the menu.
How many different deals are possible?

options.why: Added the $9$ pizzas and $6$ sides instead of multiplying their counts.
Multiplied the $9$ pizzas by the $2$ stages instead of by the $6$ sides.
Counted only the pizzas and ignored the side choices.

questions.solution_text:
There are $9$ ways to choose the pizza and $6$ ways to choose the side.
$9 \times 6$
$= 54$

questions.question_text:
A cinema snack deal is one of $8$ snacks with one of $4$ drinks.
How many different snack deals are possible?

options.why: Added the $8$ snacks and $4$ drinks instead of multiplying their counts.
Multiplied the $8$ snacks by the $2$ stages instead of by the $4$ drinks.
Counted only the drinks and ignored the snack choices.

questions.solution_text:
There are $8$ ways to choose the snack and $4$ ways to choose the drink.
$8 \times 4$
$= 32$

questions.question_text:
A car park code is one letter followed by two digits.
The letter must be a consonant ($21$ of the $26$ letters) and the code must end in a $5$ or a $0$.
Letters and digits may otherwise be repeated.
How many codes are possible?

options.why: Applied the consonant restriction but let the last digit be any of the ten digits.
Applied the last-digit restriction but allowed all $26$ letters in the first position.
Ignored both restrictions and counted every letter and every digit as available.

questions.solution_text:
There are $21$ consonants, $10$ options for the middle digit, and $2$ options for the last digit.
$21 \times 10 \times 2$
$= 420$

questions.question_text:
Lena has $7$ T-shirts and $5$ pairs of shorts, and wears one of each.
How many different outfits can she make?

options.why: Added the $7$ T-shirts and $5$ pairs of shorts instead of multiplying their counts.
Multiplied the $7$ T-shirts by the $2$ stages instead of by the $5$ pairs of shorts.
Counted only the T-shirts and ignored the shorts choices.

questions.solution_text:
Each of the $7$ T-shirts can be worn with any of the $5$ pairs of shorts.
$7 \times 5$
$= 35$

questions.question_text:
A code has $2$ letters followed by $4$ digits.
The first letter must be a vowel (A, E, I, O or U), and the last digit must be odd.
Letters and digits may otherwise be repeated.
How many different codes are possible?

options.why: Allowed all $10$ digits in the last position instead of only the $5$ odd digits.
Allowed all $26$ letters in the first position instead of only the $5$ vowels.
Counted only two unrestricted digit positions instead of three, leaving out one digit.

questions.solution_text:
The first letter has $5$ options and the second has $26$.
The first three digits each have $10$ options, and the last digit has $5$ options.
$5 \times 26 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 5$
$= 650\,000$
